solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Look to comprehend what is being said? (3-4)

definitions.text: Look to comprehend what is being said?

blocks.note: the surface reads this as a casual 'look here'; the setter means using your eyes

blocks.clueFragment: to comprehend what is being said?
blocks.note: understanding speech, which you would expect to do by ear, here done by watching a mouth move

annotation.surface: Someone straining to catch what is being said in a conversation.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is 'Look': you would expect listening to be how you understand speech, but a lip-reader does it with the eyes.
annotation.definitionFit: To lip-read is to understand speech by watching the movement of the speaker's lips.

clue.text: Capital levy initially is good for Genevans (6)

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of 'levy'
Geneva is French-speaking, so 'good' goes into French

annotation.surface: A remark about a capital tax that the Swiss of Geneva would welcome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital levy' reads as a tax on wealth, but 'Capital' alone is the definition: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Lisbon is one capital city, Portugal's, and the clue gives only the category.

clue.text: Page summing up superfluous content in article (7)

blocks.note: p is the standard abbreviation for page
adding numbers is summing them up

annotation.surface: An editor tallying up how much filler a writer has put into a piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Summing up' suggests a conclusion, but here it just means doing arithmetic.
annotation.definitionFit: Padding is material added to a piece of writing only to make it longer.

clue.text: Unopened load that is almost the equivalent of 1.25 per cent? (9)

indicators.note: a thing unopened has lost its first letter, so WEIGHT drops its W
stops one letter short, so THE loses its E

annotation.surface: A dry note about a heavy load and a small percentage, like something from a shipping manifest.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end and hides behind 'the': 1.25 per cent is one part in eighty, hence an eightieth.
annotation.definitionFit: A bit of arithmetic dressed as a definition: 100 divided by 80 gives 1.25, so one part in eighty is 1.25 per cent.

clue.text: Costly endeavour ultimately led by US drug agency (4)

indicators.note: takes the final letter of 'endeavour'
the R comes after, led by, the agency

annotation.surface: An expensive operation run by the American drug-enforcement agency.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue lists R before DEA, but 'led by' puts the agency in front.
annotation.definitionFit: Dear means expensive, as in 'petrol is dear'.

clue.text: No one story recalled great joy (7)

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: Someone telling a story in which nobody was happy, and nobody remembers it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' acts on everything before it, not just 'story', so the whole three-part string is turned round at once.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a state of intense happiness, elation carrying a sense of being lifted up.

clue.text: Where writers could be supported as cries turned to anger (10)

indicators.note: the letters of CRIES are turned about into a new order

annotation.surface: Protesters whose cries turned to anger as they stood up for writers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supported' sounds like championing a cause; in the definition it means propped up physically, as a writer leans on a writing desk.
annotation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk, where a writer's paper and elbows are supported.

clue.text: A second TV is something worth having (5)

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second

annotation.surface: A plug for owning a second television.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A second TV' reads as one item, but it splits into three pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from accounting and everyday speech: anything of value that you own or can draw on.

clue.text: Attending to some pressing work? (7)

blocks.note: the surface reads 'pressing' as urgent; the setter means flattening creases out of clothes

annotation.surface: Someone dealing with an urgent job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' wants to mean urgent; it means flattening clothes with an iron.
annotation.definitionFit: Ironing is pressing clothes, a household chore.

clue.text: Entitled people certainly not happy for the most part (8)

indicators.note: keeps most of BLESSED, dropping its last letter

annotation.surface: A grumble that people with a sense of entitlement are mostly not happy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Entitled' looks like a jibe at spoiled people, but it means literally holding titles: the nobility.
annotation.definitionFit: The noblesse are the nobility, people who hold titles.

clue.text: Team with good weapons — things you can steal, perhaps? (4,7)

blocks.note: g is the abbreviation for good

annotation.surface: A well-armed team, and what a thief might make off with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steal' suggests theft, but you 'steal a glance' by looking quickly and secretly.
annotation.definitionFit: A sidelong glance is often described as stolen, since it is taken covertly.

clue.text: Relative going round globe? (3)

indicators.note: turns BRO round so it runs backwards

annotation.surface: A family member travelling the world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going round globe' reads as circling the world; 'going round' acts on the relative and 'globe' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are poetic or formal words for a sphere, and the royal orb is a jewelled globe.

clue.text: Medical procedure I had is inducing sleep (6)

blocks.note: to have a meal is to eat it

annotation.surface: A patient saying the operation they had is making them drowsy.
annotation.walkthrough: Opiate works here as an adjective: an opiate drug is one inducing sleep.
annotation.definitionFit: As an adjective, opiate means sleep-inducing or soporific.

clue.text: Harangue horrible family in speech (8)

indicators.note: the words are to be heard, not read

blocks.note: dire is horrible and a tribe is a family group

annotation.surface: A dreadful family delivering a long rant.
annotation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'dire tribe' matches 'diatribe'.
annotation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a harangue.

clue.text: Perfect study site millions joined (10)

blocks.note: a university is a place of study
m is the abbreviation for millions

annotation.surface: An ideal location for research, where millions have signed up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perfect study' tempts you to read 'Perfect' as a verb; it is an adjective, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Unimpaired means undamaged, intact, perfect.

clue.text: Enough messed about with re: video game company’s environmental threat (10,3)

indicators.note: the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: Sega, the video game maker, with its possessive S

annotation.surface: A complaint that a games company has already done enough environmental damage.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of 'company's' is needed as a letter: SEGA'S supplies the second S.
annotation.definitionFit: Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide drive global warming, a threat to the environment.

clue.text: One following US soccer frantically around start of season (9)

indicators.note: the letters of US SOCCER are thrown about
the scrambled letters go round the S
takes the first letter of 'season'

blocks.note: anagram fodder, arranged round the S

annotation.surface: An American football club in a frantic start to its season.
annotation.walkthrough: SUC + S + CESSOR: the S from 'season' sits inside the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A successor is one who follows another.

clue.text: Go up and wait for delivery here? (8)

blocks.note: a verb: rise in number or amount
in cricket, the batter waits in the crease for the bowler's delivery

annotation.surface: Climbing stairs to wait for a parcel.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the marked line where the batter stands to face each ball, or delivery, so a batter waiting is IN CREASE.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a plain synonym for rising; the second splits the word into a cricket phrase for where a batter stands.

clue.text: Canadian maybe runs in Nice marathon, badly (5,8)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged badly, out of order

blocks.note: r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

annotation.surface: A Canadian runner struggling in a marathon on the French Riviera.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, though it only matters as letters. 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: a Canadian is one kind of North American.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'maybe': Canadians are one of several nationalities on that continent.

clue.text: Billions invested in foundation in charge of machines (7)

indicators.note: B is put inside ROOT, as money is put into something

blocks.note: the root is the foundation or base
b is the abbreviation for billions
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

annotation.surface: Billions poured into a foundation that runs machinery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invested' suggests finance, but it only puts B inside RO_OT.
annotation.definitionFit: Robotic means relating to or like machines.

clue.text: Sped up judge’s recount (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' turns the word to read from the bottom

blocks.note: to rate something is to judge it

annotation.surface: A judge's recount of votes, hurried along.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sped up' reads as accelerated; 'up' is the turnaround instruction. The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to 'recount', a verb here, not a second vote count.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when 'recount' is the verb meaning to tell events in order, not the noun for counting votes again.

clue.text: Flower in the middle shunted towards the back (6)

indicators.note: takes the central letter of 'shunted'

blocks.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower
N is the fourth of seven letters in shunted

annotation.surface: A flower in a bed, moved from the centre to the back.
annotation.walkthrough: Astern is a nautical word, meaning at or towards the back of a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Astern means behind or towards the rear of a vessel.

clue.text: Figure of fun taken in by factual counterargument (8)

indicators.note: BUTT is taken inside REAL

annotation.surface: Someone mocked, fooled by an argument built on facts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' reads as deceived; here it means held inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is an argument made to contradict another.

clue.text: Shocking thing that’s heard periodically (5)

indicators.note: takes letters at regular intervals: the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th

blocks.note: the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters, skipping the apostrophe

annotation.surface: A startling thing that you hear every so often.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heard' tempts you to look for a sound-alike, but it is only a source of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun gun that delivers an electric shock.

clue.text: Has eyes on leaving current, fancy accommodation (3,3)

indicators.note: the I departs from DESIRES

blocks.note: to have your eye on something is to desire it
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: Someone eyeing a smart house while leaving the current one.
annotation.walkthrough: A des res is British estate-agent shorthand for a 'desirable residence', an attractive home.
annotation.definitionFit: A des res is a desirable residence, an upmarket home.

clue.text: Partly swollen, sore bit of your eye (4)

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the last three letters of swollen and the first of sore

annotation.surface: A sore, swollen patch on the eye.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma between 'swollen' and 'sore' is ignored; the answer bridges the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: The lens is the transparent part of the eye that focuses light.

clue.text: The place you might see Aussie politicians play a role (3)

definitions.text: The place you might see Aussie politicians

blocks.clueFragment: The place you might see Aussie politicians
blocks.note: the Australian Capital Territory, home of Canberra and Parliament
perform a part, as on stage

annotation.surface: Australian politicians putting on a performance.
annotation.walkthrough: The ACT, the Australian Capital Territory, contains Canberra, where the federal parliament sits.
annotation.definitionFit: The ACT holds Australia's parliament, and to act is to play a role.

clue.text: Newly-constructed steps create city view, possibly (11)

indicators.note: the letters are built into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: New steps giving a fresh view of a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' flags the definition as an example: a streetscape is one kind of city view.
annotation.definitionFit: A streetscape is the view along a street, typically in a town or city.

clue.text: Called for more heart in part of curling match (7)

indicators.note: 'heart in part' says the heart sits within that part, so CORE goes inside END

blocks.note: a curling match is played in rounds called ends

annotation.surface: Spectators demanding more passion during a curling game.
annotation.walkthrough: Curling is a sport sliding stones along ice; each round is called an end.
annotation.definitionFit: To encore a performer is to call for more.

clue.text: Sudden rush concerning theatre employee (7)

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden rush

annotation.surface: A sudden rush involving a stagehand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the operating theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by workplace: the theatre meant is the hospital operating theatre, where surgeons are the staff who operate.
